newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to set up pension funds.
newsitem.headline: France to set up pension funds.

text.p: France said on Thursday it planned to introduce "retirement savings funds", or pension funds that will be run by independent managers.
The funds will complement the existing system of universal pensions.

They will be set up by one or several companies, based on agreements with their workers, or by branch sectors. People will contribute on a voluntary basis and it will be up to the companies themselves to decide whether or not to top up their employees' contributions. The funds will be managed by independent specialists, it said in a statement.
There will be no ceiling on allocation of assets by the pension funds, which will thus be free to make their own choice about how much to invest in stocks and bonds.
However, the government said it plans to modify prudential rules that currently tend to favour investment in bonds, to encourage retirement funds to invest in shares.

The government has said it wants to direct savings towards shares and longer-term productive investment in the corporate sector, boosting the Paris stock market and improving the capital base of French companies.
Management of the funds will be independent of the companies contributing to them, although there will be no rules preventing the funds reinvesting in these companies.
